reason: h15 round (2026-11-21, specs/dsl.md 'Offsets from now, relative weekends, parts of a month'): two new sealed splits, test_rel_writers (240 rows, writer set rel-w3: messages and notices by region) and test_rel_web (138 rows, rel-w4: phrases from public pages, mostly parser test suites), both deduped against all data and evals. Label-policy change: 'this weekend' is WKND+0 (was sa>su), offsets from now are now+Nh (were x), a year on an nth weekday is @YYYY-MM. 13 e16 rows that h15 reads with a new token were relabeled by two labelers who did not see h15's output: 12 relabeled, 1 dropped (unsure).
known_issues: The stale-row list was found by running h15 over the e16 rows (a row was listed when h15 answered with a new token, WKND, now, W#K or a @YYYY-MM month, and the label resolved differently on some reference day), then relabeled by two labelers who did not see h15's output. Stale rows that h15 does not read were not listed.

test_rel_web: about 80% of its phrases come from public parser test suites (duckling, dateparser, Recognizers-Text, chronic); few are from event or forum pages, because most such pages could not be fetched.

v007 train (a training set, not an eval) keeps labels that conflict with the h15 policy: 'last day of the month' as a monthly recurrence and 'this weekend' as sa>su. They are in specs/engines/h15-known-conflicts.json.

The h15 engine author read the texts of the open pool writer sets (rel-w1, rel-w2) while writing the rule, including the odd-half rows. No row of test_rel_writers or test_rel_web was read before scoring.

Post hoc: h15 was scored once on the committed engine (test_rel_writers 0.500, test_rel_web 0.732, exact). The family aggregates showed offsets from now failing on test_rel_writers (families C to F at 0.00 to 0.10), because the rule read an offset only when it was the whole text. The engine author then added a search for the offset inside a sentence and scored again (0.742, 0.739). No sealed row was read, but the fix used a failure category from the sealed split, so the second numbers are not independent and test_rel_writers is burned for further offset tuning.
